files.why: Date-range filter control for the invoice list; per rule 7 / worked example #3 two same-reason usages are duplicated in each slice's ui/, not promoted to shared/ (promotion needs 3+).
Mount the filter at the top of the invoices card and bind it to the composable's range state.
Hold the selected date range and filter the cached invoices by it (issueDate) before returning rows.
A deliberate duplicate of billing's filter (same look and behaviour) living in scheduling's ui/, because at two usages the constitution says duplicate rather than share.
Mount the filter at the top and replace the fixed single-day ref with the selected range bound to the composable.
Accept a date range instead of a single day and filter appointments by start within that range.
Add a fetchAppointmentsForRange query alongside fetchAppointmentsForDay, since the existing query filters by isSameDay only (data/ owns IO + filtering).

uncertain: Placement of the filter component: 'same look and behaviour in both' tempts a single shared/ui/date-range-picker/ primitive, but rule 7 + worked example #3 explicitly say two same-reason usages stay duplicated per-slice and only promote to shared/ at the 3rd usage. I followed the constitution and duplicated; if the team treats this as the 3rd+ same-reason usage or wants immediate promotion, it becomes shared/ui/date-range-picker/{DateRangePicker.vue,index.ts} instead of the two slice components.

Whether scheduling needs the new data/queries fetchAppointmentsForRange, or should filter client-side from fetchAppointments() inside the composable (as billing does via its cache store). I put IO/filtering in data/ to match fetchAppointmentsForDay, but the client-side variant would drop the queries.ts change.

Whether billing needs a data-layer change at all: the store already caches all invoices, so I filter in the composable and left billing/data untouched — but a fetchInvoicesInRange query in billing/data/queries.ts would be the symmetric alternative.
Whether the filter's state/logic belongs in the composable (my choice, matching existing composable patterns) or directly in the view.
questions: A 'day view' shows exactly one day, yet the request adds a date-range filter to it — should the day view become a multi-day/range view, or should the range just narrow within? This changes the view's identity and the composable signature (single Date -> range).
Which invoice date should the range filter on: issueDate, dueDate, or the appointment 'Generated from' date currently shown in the column? They filter different things.

'Same look and behaviour' — is that a hard requirement that the two filters must never diverge (argues for one shared primitive despite rule 7), or just 'consistent for now' (argues for the per-slice duplication the constitution mandates at two usages)?
Expected filter behaviour details: default range on load, inclusive/exclusive bounds, and what an empty/invalid range shows (all rows vs none)?
